results.reason: Issue 1 cites § 2.2 and the automatic five-year renewal. It quotes the 270/240-day window, calls it 30 days wide, and explains that missing it locks Harrowgate into a five-year renewal.

Issue 2 quotes § 3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates) and contrasts it with Term Sheet § 2.1's amber glass, beer, US/Canada scope. Observation A confirms the Supply Agreement supersedes the Term Sheet, so Harrowgate is bound by the broader text.

Issue 5 quotes Recital C (receipt on August 3, 2026). It calculates the § 5.4 deadline as September 2, 2026, notes the Amendment was signed September 21, 2026, and concludes the increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 3 explains that Amendment § 2.1 replaces § 11.2, removes recall costs from the carve-outs, and limits the indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims under § 9.1(c). It states that recall and product-defect/personal-injury exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

Issue 4 identifies the new § 14.4 assignment right to Affiliates and successors without consent. It does not say that nothing prevents assignment to a competitor, and it does not explain that Harrowgate remains bound by the § 14.3 consent requirement, which makes the restriction one-sided.
The response never cites Supply Agreement § 15.2 or states that written amendments take precedence over the Supply Agreement.
The response states that the § 11.1 liability cap is six months of fees, which captures the substance, though it does not specify fees paid before the claim arose.
The memo is addressed to the Partner and lists issues one by one. Each issue has a 'Where' line giving the document and section, and a 'Recommended fix'.
The response proposes specific language for a narrowed § 3.1, a restored § 11.2, a revised § 14.4, a price cap, and a new § 3.4.
The response states that the objection window lapsed on September 2 and that the increase is deemed accepted; it does not treat the window as still open.
The response states that the Term Sheet is non-binding and superseded, and that § 3.1 governs.
